title: Context-aware Event Forecasting via Graph Disentanglement

problem.claim: Event forecasting models relational and temporal patterns from historical events to forecast future events.

gap.claim: Formulating event forecasting solely as link prediction on temporal event graphs is limited because events are often coarse-grained and fixed ontologies cannot retain out-of-ontology contextual information.

narrative_sequence.summary: Event forecasting is described as a challenging task with applications in crisis alarming and disaster prevention.
The task is to model relational and temporal patterns in historical events for future forecasting.
Most existing studies formulate event forecasting as link prediction on temporal event graphs.
The structured formulation is limited by coarse-grained event types and loss of contextual information outside a fixed ontology.

unknowns: The proposed graph disentanglement method is not described.
No datasets, baselines, experimental results, or quantitative findings are supplied.
The abstract units do not establish an explicit novel contribution.
